hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: If any statement-order or declaration-order edit ever moves the numbering, 'numbering is declaration order' is wrong. Measured 2026-09-03: probe (2) moved the homing positions and six mnemonics and left all four register numbers exactly where they were, which is the cleanest possible separation of the two rules and supports rather than refutes the framing. The named next idea is refutable just as cheaply: add `parent = parent;` (or an equivalent redundant assignment) and read +0x14 - if r3 still homes into r28, first-assignment order is not the key either.

hypothesis.statement: The rotation is not source-reachable, because the two things that would have to move are governed by DIFFERENT rules and only one of them is a source variable. Probe (2) separated them: callee-saved NUMBERING is keyed to DECLARATION ORDER and is invariant under statement reordering, while HOMING POSITION follows first-use order and moves freely with it. The four defining instructions, each quoted from `fnasm.py game/mb/mb_tree MBNewNode --raw --diff` at its offset - target on the left, ours on the right: `@0x10 mr. r28,r4` against `@0x10 mr. r29,r4` (matrix); `@0x14 addi r31,r3,0` against `@0x14 addi r28,r3,0` (parent); `@0x18 addi r29,r5,0` against `@0x18 addi r30,r5,0` (type); `@0x38 lwz r30,0(0) @lbl_80344EE0` against `@0x38 lwz r31,0(0) @lbl_80344EE0` (node). Each of those four is the ONLY definition of its register in its stream. So our ascending set r28,r29,r30,r31 = parent,matrix,type,node is exactly declaration order (three parameters then the one local), while retail's r28,r29,r30,r31 = matrix,type,node,parent is that same list with `parent` moved to the END: retail's colouring is what our source would produce if `parent` were declared LAST, and `parent` is parameter 1, whose position is ABI-fixed. Probe (1) closes the one remaining way to express 'declared last': aliasing the parameter to a later-declared local, which MWCC coalesces away. The next lane's cheapest untried idea is therefore NOT another ordering edit but a probe of whether the numbering rule has a second key - whether a parameter that is ASSIGNED TO in the body is re-ranked at its assignment rather than its declaration. Note which parameters those are here: `matrix` is reassigned by `matrix = gIdentityMatrix;` (emitted at `@0x28 mr r28,r0` in target, `@0x28 mr r29,r0` in ours) and `type` by `type = 1;` (`@0x34 li r29,1` in target, `@0x34 li r30,1` in ours), while `parent` is never assigned - which would explain retail's order as first-ASSIGNMENT order and would make `parent` movable by giving it a redundant self-assignment.
